comparison: Perfect agreement on labeling methodology (C16-C19, C55). Both evaluations find the method sound and well-established. OpenEval emphasizes methodological details and internal consistency, while peer reviewers explicitly reference the 2015 validation and describe the technology as 'solid'.

Complete agreement on spatial correlation between chromatin motion restriction and replication sites (C27). Both evaluations accept this finding as supported. OpenEval highlights methodological soundness of proximity analysis, while peer reviewers list it as an accepted major conclusion.

Strong agreement on S-phase chromatin motion constraint (C20-C25). Both find the core observation supported. OpenEval notes quantitative measurements and two cell types but mentions lack of explicit p-values. Peer reviewers acknowledge the addition of IMR90 diploid cells strengthened conclusions and note 'substantially improved' quality. Peer result also includes C2 not in OpenEval result.

Both address the key experimental finding that synthesis inhibition further restricts motion (C41-C43). OpenEval R7 focuses on the experimental observation and comparison to active replication. Peer R5 also includes the mechanistic conclusion (C44, C5) and frames this as the central insight about replisome loading being independent of DNA synthesis.

Both address the main mechanistic conclusion (C5, C44) that replisome loading constrains chromatin independent of synthesis. OpenEval R8 provides detailed logical chain connecting observations to conclusion. Peer R5 also includes experimental findings (C41-C43) and identifies this as a major accepted conclusion about the counterintuitive synthesis-independence.

Both address aphidicolin effects and molecular consequences (C28-C31, C36-C37 overlap). OpenEval R4 emphasizes quantification rigor and complementary methods. Peer R4 covers broader molecular characterization including helicase and polymerase behavior (C32-C35, C38-C40) and treats all biochemical observations as established without challenge. Peer result includes C3-C4 not in OpenEval result.

Partial overlap on helicase behavior (C32-C33, C38-C39). OpenEval R5 focuses specifically on MCM2 phosphorylation and helicase activation interpretation. Peer R4 includes these claims within broader acceptance of all replisome molecular characterization without specific commentary on helicase findings.

Partial overlap on polymerase behavior (C34-C35, C40). OpenEval R6 specifically addresses differential polymerase accumulation and PCNA interactions as key supporting observations. Peer R4 includes these within general acceptance of molecular characterization but does not specifically highlight polymerase findings.

OpenEval R9 addresses literature review and established knowledge claims (C1, C6-C15, C26, C61-C67). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. These background claims were not specifically evaluated by peer reviewers as they focus on novel findings rather than literature context.

OpenEval R10 addresses established knowledge and methodological context (C45-C50, C58-C60). No corresponding peer review evaluation found. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background and methodological claims.

OpenEval R11 identifies speculative claims and cited context (C54, C56-C57) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct experimental testing. No corresponding peer review evaluation found. Peer reviewers did not specifically address these speculative or contextual claims.
